# Expression functions

<!-- GENERATED by `zig build docs-md` from the FnDoc catalog in expr.zig. Do not edit. -->

All function names are case-insensitive. Functions are grouped by purpose
below; each table sorts on a header click and filters as you type.

!!! tip "Every example below is runnable"
    Click any example to evaluate it in your browser — bxp's own
    expression engine, compiled to WebAssembly. Edit the expression in
    the panel that opens to try variations; `Esc` closes it.

## Logic & conditionals

Branch, fall back to the first non-empty value, and test membership.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IF</span>(cond, yes, no)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="IF(1 &lt; 0, 'yes', 'no')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IF</span>(<span class="hl-num">1</span> &lt; <span class="hl-num">0</span>, <span class="hl-str">'yes'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'no'</span>)</code></button> | Short-circuit conditional. Returns `yes` if `cond` is truthy, else `no`. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CASE</span>(expr, m<span class="hl-num">1</span>, r<span class="hl-num">1</span>, …, default)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="CASE('B', 'B', 'BUY', 'S', 'SELL', '?')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CASE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'B'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'B'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'S'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'SELL'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'?'</span>)</code></button> | Multi-branch mapping. Compares `expr` against each `m`/`r` pair in order and returns the first matching `r`; returns the trailing `default` when nothing matches (or "" if no default is given). Equality matches the `=` operator (numeric when both sides parse as numbers, else byte-exact string). Only the selected result is evaluated. Collapses nested `IF(IF(IF(…)))` chains. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IFERROR</span>(expr, fallback)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="IFERROR(YEAR('not-a-date'), '')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IFERROR</span>(YEAR(<span class="hl-str">'not-a-date'</span>), <span class="hl-str">''</span>)</code></button> | Return `expr`'s value, or `fallback` if evaluating `expr` raises a data error (not-a-number, bad date, numeric overflow). `fallback` is evaluated only on error. Template errors — unknown function, wrong argument count, syntax — are NOT caught: IFERROR guards against messy data, not template mistakes. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">COALESCE</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="COALESCE('', 'fallback')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">COALESCE</span>(<span class="hl-str">''</span>, <span class="hl-str">'fallback'</span>)</code></button> | First non-empty argument (empty = whitespace-only string). Returns last argument verbatim as fallback. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NULLIF</span>(value, sentinel)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="NULLIF('N/A', 'N/A')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NULLIF</span>(<span class="hl-str">'N/A'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'N/A'</span>)</code></button> | Return `""` when `value` equals `sentinel`, otherwise return `value`. Equality is numeric when both sides parse as numbers, otherwise byte-exact string compare — mirrors the `=` operator. Typical use: collapse sentinel values such as `"-9999"`, `"\N"`, `"N/A"` to empty. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IN</span>(value, v<span class="hl-num">1</span>, v<span class="hl-num">2</span>, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="IN('BUY', 'BUY', 'SELL')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IN</span>(<span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'SELL'</span>)</code></button> | Return "true" when `value` equals any of `v1, v2, …`. Equality is numeric when both sides parse as numbers, otherwise byte-exact string compare — mirrors the `=` operator. Variadic 2+ args. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ISEMPTY</span>(x)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="ISEMPTY('  ')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ISEMPTY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'  '</span>)</code></button> | Return "true" when `x` is empty or whitespace-only, else "false". The safe emptiness test: a bare `x = ''` wrongly matches `'0'` (which coerces to empty in numeric context), whereas ISEMPTY checks the trimmed string length. |

## Text

Trim, case-fold, slice, pad, search, and measure strings.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">TRIM</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="TRIM('  hello  ')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">TRIM</span>(<span class="hl-str">'  hello  '</span>)</code></button> | Strip leading and trailing whitespace from a string. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SPLIT_PART</span>(s, delim, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="SPLIT_PART('AAPL.US', '.', 1)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SPLIT_PART</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.'</span>, <span class="hl-num">1</span>)</code></button> | Return the n-th part of `s` split by `delim` (1-based index). Returns "" when n exceeds the part count, when `delim` is empty, or when `n` ≤ 0. When `delim` is not found, n=1 returns the whole string and n&gt;1 returns "". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CONTAINS</span>(haystack, needle)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="CONTAINS('Apple Inc', 'Inc')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CONTAINS</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Apple Inc'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Inc'</span>)</code></button> | Returns "true" if `haystack` contains `needle`, else "false". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEFT</span>(s, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LEFT('AAPL.US', 4)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEFT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">4</span>)</code></button> | Return the first `n` bytes of `s`. `n` is clamped to `[0, len(s)]`; negative `n` returns "". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RIGHT</span>(s, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="RIGHT('AAPL.US', 2)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RIGHT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code></button> | Return the last `n` bytes of `s`. `n` is clamped to `[0, len(s)]`; negative `n` returns "". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SUBSTR</span>(s, start, length)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="SUBSTR('AAPL.US', 1, 4)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SUBSTR</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">1</span>, <span class="hl-num">4</span>)</code></button> | Return `length` bytes from `s` starting at 1-based position `start`. Returns "" when `start` is non-positive / past end of `s`, or when `length` is negative. `length` is clamped to the bytes remaining from `start`. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">UPPER</span>(s)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="UPPER('aapl')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">UPPER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'aapl'</span>)</code></button> | Full-Unicode upper-case conversion: works across Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, etc. (café → CAFÉ, ß → SS); unicameral scripts (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) pass through unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LOWER</span>(s)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LOWER('AAPL')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LOWER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL'</span>)</code></button> | Full-Unicode lower-case conversion: works across Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, etc. (CAFÉ → café, Я → я); unicameral scripts (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) pass through unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">UNACCENT</span>(s)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="UNACCENT('Café Crème')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">UNACCENT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Café Crème'</span>)</code></button> | Strip diacritics from Latin text (café → cafe, ÀÉÎ → AEI, ß → ss, ø → o). Latin-scope like Postgres unaccent: non-Latin letters keep their base script (Greek Ά → Α, not A) and CJK/Arabic pass through unchanged; ligatures are NOT folded. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">STARTS_WITH</span>(s, prefix)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="STARTS_WITH('US123', 'US')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">STARTS_WITH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'US123'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'US'</span>)</code></button> | Return "true" when `s` begins with `prefix` (case-sensitive byte match), else "false". An empty `prefix` always matches. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ENDS_WITH</span>(s, suffix)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="ENDS_WITH('AAPL.PR', '.PR')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ENDS_WITH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.PR'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.PR'</span>)</code></button> | Return "true" when `s` ends with `suffix` (case-sensitive byte match), else "false". An empty `suffix` always matches. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEN</span>(s)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LEN('hello')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEN</span>(<span class="hl-str">'hello'</span>)</code></button> | Byte length of `s` (UTF-8 byte count, not codepoint or grapheme count). Empty string → 0. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LPAD</span>(s, len, pad)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LPAD('42', 5, '0')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LPAD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'42'</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>, <span class="hl-str">'0'</span>)</code></button> | Left-pad `s` with the `pad` string (repeated, then clipped) until it is `len` bytes long. If `s` is already `len` or longer it is truncated to the first `len` bytes; an empty `pad` returns `s` unchanged. `len` is clamped to [0, 65535]. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte count). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RPAD</span>(s, len, pad)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="RPAD('42', 5, ' ')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RPAD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'42'</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>, <span class="hl-str">' '</span>)</code></button> | Right-pad `s` with the `pad` string (repeated, then clipped) until it is `len` bytes long. If `s` is already `len` or longer it is truncated to the first `len` bytes; an empty `pad` returns `s` unchanged. `len` is clamped to [0, 65535]. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte count). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">POSITION</span>(needle, haystack)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="POSITION('Inc', 'Apple Inc')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">POSITION</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Inc'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Apple Inc'</span>)</code></button> | 1-based byte position of the first occurrence of `needle` inside `haystack`, or 0 when not found. An empty `needle` returns 1. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte offset), case-sensitive. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PROPER</span>(s)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="PROPER('apple inc')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PROPER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'apple inc'</span>)</code></button> | Title-case `s`: upper-case the first letter of every word and lower-case the rest (`apple inc` → `Apple Inc`, `o'brien` → `O'Brien`). Words break on any non-letter (spaces, digits, punctuation), like Excel PROPER. Full-Unicode via the same case tables as UPPER/LOWER; invalid UTF-8 passes through. |

## Pattern matching

Linear-time (ReDoS-safe) regular-expression match and extract.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_MATCH</span>(s, pattern)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="REGEX_MATCH('AAPL US Equity', '[A-Z]+')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_MATCH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL US Equity'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'[A-Z]+'</span>)</code></button> | Returns "true" if regular-expression `pattern` matches anywhere in `s`, else "false". `pattern` is a regex literal: anchors `^ $`, classes `[...]`, quantifiers `* + ? {m,n}`, groups, and alternation `\|` — linear-time (no backreferences or lookaround). Unicode-scalar mode is on, so `.` and class ranges span whole code points, but `\d`/`\w`/`\s` stay ASCII — match accented letters with an explicit class like `[A-ZÁ-Ž]`. Pay for the cheapest tool that does the job: CONTAINS for a literal substring, IN/REMAP for whole-value sets, regex only for a real pattern. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_EXTRACT</span>(s, pattern)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="REGEX_EXTRACT('Qualified Dividend AAPL 100', '[A-Z]{2,}')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_EXTRACT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Qualified Dividend AAPL 100'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'[A-Z]{2,}'</span>)</code></button> | Returns the first part of `s` that regular-expression `pattern` matches, or "" if there is no match. When `pattern` has a capture group `(...)`, the first group's text is returned; otherwise the whole match is returned. `pattern` is a regex literal (same syntax + Unicode notes as REGEX_MATCH): linear-time, no backreferences or lookaround, and accented letters need an explicit class like `[A-ZÁ-Ž]` (not `\w`). Use it to pull a ticker, code, or token a literal REPLACE/SPLIT_PART cannot isolate. |

## Lookup & mapping

Whole-value remap, substring replace, and `pre_pass` table lookups.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REMAP</span>(s, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span> &#124; k, v, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="REMAP('VOW.DE', 'VOW.DE', 'VOW.DE.XETRA')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REMAP</span>(<span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE.XETRA'</span>)</code></button> | Whole-value lookup: if `s` exactly equals a map key, return that key's value, else return `s` unchanged. Named form REMAP(s, 'mapname') resolves a `maps` registry entry; inline form REMAP(s, k1,v1, k2,v2, ...) gives the pairs directly. The whole-value sibling of REPLACE (which matches substrings) — use it to remap broker symbols, codes or enum values. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LOOKUP</span>([name,] key, field)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LOOKUP('AAPL', 'name')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LOOKUP</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span>)</code></button> | Retrieve a value stored by a pre_pass table. 3-arg form `LOOKUP(name, key, field)` selects the named pre_pass block. 2-arg form `LOOKUP(key, field)` works only when exactly one pre_pass block is defined. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REPLACE</span>(s, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span> &#124; from, to, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="REPLACE('1 234,56', ' ', '', ',', '.')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REPLACE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'1 234,56'</span>, <span class="hl-str">' '</span>, <span class="hl-str">''</span>, <span class="hl-str">','</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.'</span>)</code></button> | Replace substrings in `s`. Named form REPLACE(s, 'mapname') applies a `maps` registry entry's pairs. Inline single-pair REPLACE(s, from, to) replaces every occurrence of `from` with `to` (case-sensitive byte match, so multi-byte UTF-8 needles work — this is substring replace, not char-by-char). Inline variadic REPLACE(s, from1, to1, from2, to2, ...) applies the pairs in one left-to-right pass: at each position the first pair (in declared order) whose `from` matches wins and the emitted `to` is not re-scanned, so one pass replaces several tokens at once without nesting. An empty `from` matches nothing. Whole-value sibling: REMAP. |

## Numbers & money

Exact fixed-point arithmetic, rounding, min/max, and price parsing.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ABS</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="ABS(-12.5)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ABS</span>(-<span class="hl-num">12.5</span>)</code></button> | Absolute numeric value. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ROUND</span>(f, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="ROUND(3.14159, 2)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ROUND</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.14159</span>, <span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code></button> | Round `f` to `n` decimal places (half away from zero, like Excel: `ROUND(2.5,0)=3`). `n=0` rounds to the nearest integer; `n<0` rounds to tens/hundreds/etc. (`n=-2` → nearest 100); `n>=12` is a no-op (12 is the fixed-point scale). `n` is clamped to ±30. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FLOOR</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="FLOOR(3.7)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FLOOR</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.7</span>)</code></button> | Round `f` down to nearest integer. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CEILING</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="CEILING(3.2)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CEILING</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.2</span>)</code></button> | Round `f` up to nearest integer. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RAND</span>(n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="RAND(8)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RAND</span>(<span class="hl-num">8</span>)</code></button> | A string of exactly `n` random digits (each position 0–9, except the first which is 1–9 so a leading zero can't be dropped by a downstream numeric import). Use it for synthetic IDs; `n` is clamped to [1, 65]. Cryptographically seeded — not for security tokens. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_VALUE</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="PRICE_VALUE('$1,234.56')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_VALUE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'$1,234.56'</span>)</code></button> | Strip currency symbol or code from a price string, return the numeric part (e.g. "$88744.27" → "88744.27", "€24.00" → "24.00", "24.00 CZK" → "24.00"). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_CURRENCY</span>(f)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="PRICE_CURRENCY('$1,234.56')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_CURRENCY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'$1,234.56'</span>)</code></button> | Extract currency code from a price string (e.g. "EUR", "USD"). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">GREATEST</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="GREATEST(3, 7, 5)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">GREATEST</span>(<span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>)</code></button> | Largest numeric value among arguments. Per-row maximum (not aggregation across rows). Arguments are coerced to numbers; empty string coerces to 0, non-numeric strings raise an error. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEAST</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="LEAST(3, 7, 5)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEAST</span>(<span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>)</code></button> | Smallest numeric value among arguments. Per-row minimum (not aggregation across rows). Arguments are coerced to numbers; empty string coerces to 0, non-numeric strings raise an error. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">MOD</span>(a, b)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="MOD(7, 3)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">MOD</span>(<span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">3</span>)</code></button> | Remainder of `a` divided by `b`, with the sign of the dividend `a` (truncated division, like SQL/C `%`: `MOD(-7, 3) = -1`). `MOD(a, 0)` returns "" (mirrors the `/` operator's silent divide-by-zero). Exact over the fixed-point decimal core. |

## Dates & time

Reformat, shift, diff, and decompose dates — business-day aware.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NOW</span>()</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="NOW()"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NOW</span>()</code></button> | Current UTC datetime as ISO 8601 string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATE_CONVERT</span>(f, from, to)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="DATE_CONVERT('31.12.2024', 'DD.MM.YYYY', 'YYYY-MM-DD')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATE_CONVERT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'31.12.2024'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'DD.MM.YYYY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'YYYY-MM-DD'</span>)</code></button> | Reformat a date/time string. Format tokens: YYYY (year), MM/M (month), MMM/MMMM (month name), DD/D (day), hh/h (hour), mm/m (minute), ss/s (second), [literal] (literal characters), [*] (wildcard). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">TO_UTC</span>(ts, from)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="TO_UTC('2024-03-15T14:23:01+02:00', 'YYYY-MM-DD[T]hh:mm:ssZZ')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">TO_UTC</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15T14:23:01+02:00'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'YYYY-MM-DD[T]hh:mm:ssZZ'</span>)</code></button> | Normalise an offset-bearing timestamp to UTC. `from` is a datefmt format including the `ZZ` offset token (`+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM`) or a literal `Z`; the parsed offset is subtracted, yielding `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss` in UTC. Needs no timezone database — the offset is read from the string itself. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">TZ_OFFSET</span>(datetime, zone)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="TZ_OFFSET('2024-07-15 12:00:00', 'Europe/Prague')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">TZ_OFFSET</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-07-15 12:00:00'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Europe/Prague'</span>)</code></button> | UTC offset (`+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM`) of IANA `zone` at local wall-clock `datetime` (`YYYY-MM-DD[ hh:mm:ss]`), DST-aware. Append it to a naive local timestamp to make it ISO-8601 tz-aware. Unknown zone → "". Within the one-hour DST-transition window the input is read as local time, so the result can be off by the offset. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">TZ_CONVERT</span>(ts, from_zone, to_zone)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="TZ_CONVERT('2024-07-15 12:00:00', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/Prague')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">TZ_CONVERT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-07-15 12:00:00'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'America/New_York'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Europe/Prague'</span>)</code></button> | Convert wall-clock `ts` (`YYYY-MM-DD[ hh:mm:ss]`) from `from_zone` to `to_zone`, returning `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss`. Each zone is an IANA id (`Europe/Prague`), a fixed offset (`+02:00`), or `UTC`. Full DST-aware IANA conversion via the bundled tzdata. Unknown zone → "". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IS_DST</span>(datetime, zone)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="IS_DST('2024-07-15 12:00:00', 'Europe/Prague')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IS_DST</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-07-15 12:00:00'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Europe/Prague'</span>)</code></button> | "true" when daylight-saving time is in effect in IANA `zone` at local wall-clock `datetime` (`YYYY-MM-DD[ hh:mm:ss]`), else "false". An unknown or fixed-offset zone → "false". |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATEADD</span>(d, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="DATEADD('2024-01-31', 7)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATEADD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-31'</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>)</code></button> | Add `n` calendar days to date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD). Negative `n` subtracts. Returns YYYY-MM-DD. For business-day arithmetic (skipping weekends) use WORKDAY(). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATEDIFF</span>(d<span class="hl-num">1</span>, d<span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="DATEDIFF('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATEDIFF</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-01'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'2024-12-31'</span>)</code></button> | Calendar days from `d2` to `d1`: positive when `d1` is later. Both arguments are YYYY-MM-DD strings. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">WORKDAY</span>(d, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="WORKDAY('2024-01-01', 10)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">WORKDAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-01'</span>, <span class="hl-num">10</span>)</code></button> | Add `n` business days to date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD), skipping Saturdays and Sundays. Negative `n` subtracts. Correct for T+2 settlement math; does NOT account for exchange holidays. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">YEAR</span>(d)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="YEAR('2024-03-15')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">YEAR</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code></button> | Year component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">MONTH</span>(d)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="MONTH('2024-03-15')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">MONTH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code></button> | Month component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number, 1-12. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DAY</span>(d)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="DAY('2024-03-15')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code></button> | Day-of-month component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number, 1-31. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">WEEKDAY</span>(d)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="WEEKDAY('2024-03-15')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">WEEKDAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code></button> | ISO day-of-week for date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD): Monday=1 … Sunday=7. Useful for weekend-trade detection: `WEEKDAY([Date]) > 5`. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">EOMONTH</span>(d)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="EOMONTH('2024-02-10')"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">EOMONTH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-02-10'</span>)</code></button> | Last calendar day of the month containing date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD), as YYYY-MM-DD. Useful for snapping coupon/dividend dates and month-end reporting. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NTH_DOW</span>(year, month, weekday, n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="NTH_DOW(2024, 3, 7, -1)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NTH_DOW</span>(<span class="hl-num">2024</span>, <span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, -<span class="hl-num">1</span>)</code></button> | Date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the `n`-th `weekday` (ISO Mon=1 … Sun=7) in `year`/`month`. Positive `n` counts from the start (1 = first); negative counts from the end (-1 = last). Returns "" when the occurrence doesn't exist or an argument is out of range. Handy for DST boundaries — EU summer time is `NTH_DOW(YEAR(d), 3, 7, -1)` (last Sunday of March) to `NTH_DOW(YEAR(d), 10, 7, -1)` (last Sunday of October). |

## Row & source context

Values drawn from the current row's position and its source file.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FIELDS</span>(n)</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="FIELDS(2)"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FIELDS</span>(<span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code></button> | Field value by 1-based column index. n must be a positive integer — use this when the column header is unknown or unstable; use the [ColumnName] syntax to look up by header name. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FILENAME</span>()</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="FILENAME()"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FILENAME</span>()</code></button> | Input file stem — the file name with its directory and the matched `file_pattern_in` suffix removed (the same stem used for output naming). Broker exports often encode account/broker/period in the name, so e.g. `SPLIT_PART(FILENAME(), '_', 3)` extracts a field from it. Empty during stateless evaluation (no source file). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RECORD_NUM</span>()</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="RECORD_NUM()"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RECORD_NUM</span>()</code></button> | 1-based input record number of the current row within the file (the first data row is 1). Use it for synthetic IDs, dedup keys, or skip-first-N logic. 0 during stateless evaluation and inside the pre_pass scan. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SHEET_NAME</span>()</code><br><button type="button" class="bxp-try" data-bxp-expr="SHEET_NAME()"><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SHEET_NAME</span>()</code></button> | For xlsx-derived input, the configured `xlsx_sheet.name` the row came from; "" for native CSV/JSON input and during stateless evaluation. |
